Implants can replace single or multiple missing teeth with a natural look and strong bite, provided your gums and jawbone are healthy. We’ll review your medical history, 3D imaging, and habits (like smoking) to confirm candidacy. Helps prevent bone loss and shifting of nearby teeth. High long-term success with good home care and checkups. May require bone graft or sinus lift in low-bone areas. AAOMS — Dental Implants NIDCR — Dental Implants What’s the difference between traditional dentures and implant-supported dentures? Traditional dentures rest on the gums, while implant-supported options “snap” to dental implants for stability. Many patients report better chewing, speech, and comfort with fewer sore spots. Lower dentures benefit most from implant retention. Removable (snap-in) vs. fixed (screw-retained “All-on-X”). Still requires regular cleanings and maintenance. ADA MouthHealthy — Dentures NCBI — Implant Overdentures (overview) How long do crowns and bridges last? With proper home care and regular visits, many crowns and bridges last 10–15 years or longer. Nightguards, good flossing under bridges, and avoiding very hard foods can extend their lifespan. Porcelain, zirconia, and metal options to fit needs. Address clenching/grinding to reduce fracture risk. Routine x-rays help monitor margins and decay risk. ADA — Dental Crowns ADA — Dental Bridges Is professional teeth whitening safe, and will it work for me? When supervised by a dentist, whitening is considered safe and effective for natural enamel. It won’t lighten crowns, veneers, or fillings, and we’ll screen for causes of discoloration first. Short-term sensitivity is common and manageable. Custom trays help maintain results with less gum irritation. Avoid strong pigments (coffee/wine) for 24–48 hours after. ADA — Teeth Whitening FDA — Teeth Whitening Do you offer same-day or ceramic restorations? Many practices use digital scanners and in-office milling to deliver strong, tooth-colored restorations in one visit. Candidates are selected based on tooth structure, bite, and fracture risk. No messy impressions; faster turnaround. Precise fit from CAD/CAM workflows. Nightguard recommended for heavy grinders. ADA — Evidence-Based Dentistry Cochrane — Ceramic restorations (evidence) What options do you have for dental anxiety or sensitive gag reflex? We tailor comfort with calming communication, numbing gels, nitrous oxide (“laughing gas”), and—when appropriate—oral conscious or IV sedation. Your medical history and medications guide safe choices. Nitrous wears off quickly; you can usually drive yourself. Oral/IV sedation requires an escort and pre-op fasting. We screen for sleep apnea, heart, or respiratory issues. ADA — Sedation ADA Science & Research What does recovery look like after extractions or implant surgery? Most patients experience mild swelling and soreness for 2–3 days; stitches are often removed in about a week. Implants typically need a few months to fuse (osseointegrate) before final teeth are attached. Cold compresses and head elevation help with swelling. Soft diet; avoid straws/smoking to protect healing sites. Call us for increasing pain, fever, or unusual bleeding. AAOMS — Post-Op Instructions CDC — Oral Health Basics *This information is educational and not medical advice. Your dentist will recommend personalized care after an exam. Implants Over Dentures   Arizona Dental offers implant overdentures as a cost-effective alternative to traditional dentures and implants. Implant overdentures are a stable, permanent solution for replacing your missing teeth. Call us at (602) 788-4040 to schedule your consultation with Dr. Joe Gerard, and to learn more about implant overdentures in Phoenix and Sun City, Arizona. There Are Many Benefits To Overdenture Implants: Cost-Effective Durability Longevity Noted Comfort Seamless Fit Complete Correction Confident Usage Want to learn more? Please contact our office today for more information on implant overdentures and to schedule your appointment with our dentist. The Overdenture Implant Process When you receive implant overdentures, our dentist begins by taking impressions. These impressions help us determine the correct positioning of the teeth on your new dentures, and confirm the best location for each implant. They are also used to ensure that you receive the correct bite and a natural-looking appearance. We often provide a copy of your impression for your surgeon as guidance during your implant placement procedure. The Science Behind Implant Overdentures An implant overdenture, also known as an implant-supported denture or snap-on denture, fits over your dental implants to provide your restoration with greater stability. Implant overdentures are used to replace the teeth in a full arch when all of your teeth are missing. This restoration “snaps” into place to offer you greater comfort and an improved chewing ability, and is removable to make it easier to clean both your dentures and the dental implants that support them. Often, an upper overdenture will require more implants for support than a lower overdenture. Depending on your needs, it may be possible to create an upper denture without a palate (roof of the mouth). Our dentist will discuss with you which type of overdenture will best meet your needs during your consultation. If you have questions about caring for your teeth, we invite you to come see Dr. Joe Gerard at Arizona Dental. Our dentist would be happy to provide professional and customized advice on maintaining your dental hygiene in Phoenix and Sun City, Arizona. You are welcome to call our office at (602) 788-4040 to schedule an appointment. Our dentist recommends that you follow these basic steps to help your smile stay in optimal health: Floss at least once every day. The most important time to floss is just before you go to sleep at night. Eat a balanced diet. Limiting your intake of very sugary and acidic foods can help to prevent tooth decay. Brush your teeth after each meal or at least twice a day. We encourage you to use a soft-bristled toothbrush and a toothpaste that includes fluoride. Dental Hygiene Is An Ongoing Effort During your time at our office, our team works hard to improve your oral health. It is essential, however, that you continue taking care of your smile at home through consistent oral hygiene. Good dental hygiene includes a number of daily habits and practices that help to keep your smile healthy and bright. Consistent Dental Hygiene Maintain your regular visits to the dentist every six months. During these visits, we will provide a professional teeth cleaning and a thorough dental exam to make certain we provide any needed preventive or restorative treatments. When you visit our dentist and team, we will review your dental hygiene habits with you and offer needed information on any additional steps you can take to further improve your oral health. To learn more about dental hygiene and to schedule your next appointment at our office, we welcome you to call or visit us today. Routine Cleaning   Dental Cleaning & Exams Dental cleanings and exams are two of the most basic yet important preventive treatments we provide at our office. Each time you visit our dental practice for a checkup, we will provide a professional teeth cleaning and dental exam to help your smile stay healthy. Routine dental checkups focus on maintaining your smile’s optimal health and addressing any developing concerns. We encourage you to visit Arizona Dental on a regular basis for dental exams and teeth cleanings in Phoenix and Sun City, Arizona. If you are showing signs of gum disease, we may perform a medicated cleaning called scaling and root planing to remove plaque and tartar buildup. You can schedule your next visit with our dentist, Dr. Joe Gerard by calling our office at (602) 788-4040 . During your teeth cleaning and exam, our dental team will: Floss and polish your teeth for a healthy, bright smile. Examine your smile for signs of any damaging dental conditions or diseases. Clean your teeth by removing any plaque or tartar (also called dental calculus), which can lead to tooth decay and periodontal disease.     How We Can Help We utilize dental X-rays to further evaluate your smile and make certain that you receive the dental care you need. Regular dental cleanings and exams are essential in maintaining good oral health, preventing cavities and gum disease, and making sure that any damaging conditions are treated as early as possible. Our dentist recommends that you visit us every six months for a routine dental cleaning and exam. We may suggest more frequent visits if needed, and we also encourage you to contact us if you suffer from a dental emergency, pain, or injury. To schedule your next appointment, we invite you to contact us today. We look forward to caring for your smile! Cavity Prevention   Granted most anyone will agree, maintaining one’s cavity prevention is an absolute must for a variety of reasons. Not only does upholding an emphasis on consistent & effective oral/dental hygiene promote a happy & confident smile but proper cavity prevention (or lack thereof) also has a tremendous impact on the smiler’s overall health as well. For instance, without proper oral care to uphold ideal cavity prevention, it’s all but inevitable that the teeth, tongue, gum line, and the mouth in general will experience severely detrimental effects. Including tooth plaque, decay & eventual loss, periodontal/gum disease(s) such as gingivitis or periodontitis, halitosis (bad breath), cavities, and in serious cases, the always-concerning onset of oral cancer(s). There are several proven methods of cavity prevention, including: Consistent Brushing (3x per day) Daily Flossing (1-2x per day) Rinse Mouth Often (6+ per day) Reduce Sugary Foods & Beverages Limit Acidic Foods & Beverages Avoid Sipping (water excluded) Schedule Routine Dental Visits Adhere To Prescribed Dental Treatments Learn More About Cavity Prevention We encourage all patients to maintain proper oral care, hygiene, and general upkeep practices to ensure a noteworthy smile for decades to come! However, we understand that no two smiles are the same and by extension; no two oral care or treatment plans are likely to be identical as well. This is why we often cater specified dental hygiene regiments to each patient individually; thus bettering the effectiveness of cavity prevention. Contact us for additional questions. Effective Cavity Prevention While each set of teeth, gum lines, tongue, mouth, and overall smile can vary drastically from one patient to the next, it’s largely inarguable that each and every person can and will benefit from sustained cavity prevention and maintaining an active routine of oral care habits. These routine methods of cavity prevention and proactive oral care can include brushing, flossing, oral rinsing/gargling, general dental cleanliness, and periodic check-up visits to a licensed dentist.
